moat_against: Generative AI commoditizes parts of design work, threatens seat counts and raises compute costs
Adobe retains Creative Cloud bundle, distribution and a far larger revenue base to subsidize Express/Firefly
Canva owns the non-designer segment (265M MAU), made Affinity free and is pushing upmarket
Premium seat pricing ($45/editor Organization tier) invites counter-positioning; no owned OS/browser/distribution channel
moat_for: 80-90% share of professional UI/UX design; Adobe's abandoned $20B acquisition is market testimony
Customer-built design systems and component libraries — switching costs accumulate inside Figma files
Multiplayer collaboration across designers, developers and PMs; 95% of Fortune 500 use it
136% net dollar retention and expansion into paid AI credits (>80% of $10K+ customers consuming weekly)
10,000+ plugin ecosystem; Dev Mode, Make and Sites widen the surface competitors must match
moat_justification: Strong: estimated 80-90% share of professional UI/UX design, customer-built design-system switching costs, multiplayer collaboration across whole organizations (95% of Fortune 500), 136% net dollar retention and successful expansion into paid AI credits, 10,000+ plugin ecosystem. Against: generative AI threatens seat counts and raises compute costs, Adobe's Creative Cloud bundle and distribution, Canva's free Affinity suite pushing upmarket, premium seat pricing inviting counter-positioning, and no owned distribution channel.
name: Figma, Inc.
one_liner: Category-defining design platform, moat 7/10, growing 41-48% with 136% NDR and ~$1.7B cash and marketable securities — but owner's earnings are negative under every filed base (TTM -$2.74/share as reported; -$0.89/share even excluding the $975.7M one-time IPO RSU catch-up) because recurring SBC runs ~$700M/yr against ~$249M of TTM operating cash flow; it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at any price on an OE DCF until SBC falls below ~$232M/yr or cash generation roughly triples.
